definitions.explanation: A piece of cloth or knitted fabric worn around the neck for warmth. A slightly old-fashioned or literary word; マフラー is more common in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: ⟦{寒|さむ}い→寒い：00664_samui⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{襟巻|えりま}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{巻|ま}いた→巻く：02418_maku⟧。
examples.english: It was cold, so I wrapped a scarf around my neck.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{毛糸|けいと}→毛糸：00212_keito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{襟巻|えりま}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{編|あ}んで→編む：00002_amu⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother knitted a woolen scarf for me.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧{襟巻|えりま}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{雪|ゆき}だるま→雪だるま：10974_yukidaruma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}っていた→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: A snowman wearing a red scarf was standing in the yard.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of ⟦{襟|えり}→襟：06487_eri⟧ (collar/neck) and {巻|ま}き (wrapping). Considered slightly old-fashioned — younger speakers tend to use ⟦マフラー→マフラー：04533_mafuraa⟧ instead. Still common in literature, descriptions of traditional clothing, and among older speakers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {襟巻|えりま}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{巻|ま}く→巻く：02418_maku⟧ (to wrap a scarf around one's neck)
- {襟巻|えりま}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{外|はず}す→外す：02394_hazusu⟧ (to take off a scarf)
- ⟦{毛皮|けがわ}→毛皮：00205_kegawa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{襟巻|えりま}き (a fur stole)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦マフラー→マフラー：04533_mafuraa⟧: muffler, scarf — the modern, everyday word
- ⟦ストール→ストール：24219_sutooru⟧: stole — a wider, fashion-oriented wrap for the shoulders
